title: Choose the visual world for www.routecool.com
question: The roll assigned the Street Atlas. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Street Atlas
options.lineage: Spiral-bound metro street atlases that lived on the dash of every service truck before GPS
options.thesis: Every company gets its own page in the book: its own domain, database and backups, mapped like a street atlas.
materials: page-number boxes and A–H / 1–8 grid margins
options.viewport: A full-bleed atlas page of a square-mile street grid, with a tech's day drawn as one sky-blue route through stops 1–6, the headline set as the page title and a legend box holding $199/mo · 5 users · demo@routecool.com.
options.risk: Can tip into a novelty map theme if the grid, page numbers and index aren't doing real wayfinding work.

raised.raise: The day's route is one continuous line that threads every page, never chopped into decorative bits.
Every page carries a direct address (page + grid) and every cross-reference is a real link, like the app's every-screen-is-a-URL.
Sky blue is reserved for the live route and the action; nothing else wears it.
One unvarying line weight across map, icons and UI; no shadows, no gradients.
Newest is darkest: the leg ahead is full ink, completed legs drop to tint.

options.label: Equipment Data Plate
options.lineage: The riveted nameplate on every condenser and furnace that a tech reads on every call
options.thesis: Your RouteCool stamped like the nameplate on your own unit: model, serial, your domain, your database.
options.viewport: One big nameplate fills the screen: MODEL RouteCool · SERIAL kappaair.routecool.com · RATED 5 users · $199/mo, with the dispatch board beneath it.
options.risk: The most familiar HVAC-industrial move; metal texture can turn skeuomorphic and heavy.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: Each section is a decision point with one clear arrow: your data, this way.
options.viewport: A yellow overhead band: Your own database, Your own domain, $199/mo up to 5 users, with numbers at gate scale.
options.case: Holds product clarity (very legible) but HVAC owners don't identify with airports the way they do with the truck's map book.
options.risk: Generic signage pastiche if the band system isn't strict.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.thesis: The product as numbered broadcast pages.
options.viewport: P100 index with features as numbered pages.
options.case: Loses both axes: retro-tech novelty, far from the trades.
options.kept: Every page has a direct address, so the atlas uses page + grid references as real links.

options.label: Hand-bent Neon Circuit
options.viewport: The wordmark as one lit tube.
options.case: Loses both: dark glow reads nightlife, not field service.
options.kept: One continuous line: the route threads every page unbroken.

options.label: Crank Paper Menagerie
options.viewport: Figures marching across a crank line.
options.case: Loses both: whimsical, unrelated to dispatch.
options.kept: One color reserved for what's in motion: sky blue only on the live route and the action.

options.label: Ligne Claire Album
options.thesis: Everything drawn in one even line.
options.viewport: A comic tier of a tech's day.
options.case: Loses both: charming, but comics undercut a $199/mo business tool.
options.kept: One unvarying line weight everywhere; flat fills, no shading.

options.label: Suminagashi Ink Basin
options.thesis: The page as a fluid surface.
options.case: Loses both: meditative art piece, zero trade identity.
options.kept: Newest is darkest: the leg ahead is full ink, finished legs fade.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean SaaS landing page in RouteCool sky blue, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Headline + demo button on the left, the dispatch board screenshot on the right, feature grid and pricing below.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other field-service suite by design.
